```{python}
#| label: fig-dft-coverage
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Stuck-at fault coverage of random test vectors for the 8-bit `bs_reg`, with its flip-flops cut into inputs and outputs, simulated by Fault with `-v 10 -r 10`, i.e., in batches of 10 vectors. Most faults are detected within the first 50 vectors. From 350 vectors on, all 1156 faults that the fault model of Fault can detect are found. The other 4 of the 1160 faults are untestable, so the coverage stays at 99.66 %."
#| fig-alt: "Step chart with the number of random test vectors from 0 to 500 on the horizontal axis and fault coverage from 80 to 100 percent on the vertical axis. The coverage starts at 82.1 percent after 10 vectors, rises steeply to 96 percent at 50 vectors and 97.8 percent at 100, then in small steps to 99.4 percent at 190 vectors, and jumps to 99.66 percent at 350 vectors, where it stays. A dashed line at 99.66 percent is labeled all faults that Fault can detect."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Coverage in % after 10, 20, ..., 500 random vectors (Fault 0.9.4)
cov = [82.069, 89.914, 91.724, 95.086, 96.034, 96.897, 97.241, 97.500,
       97.759, 97.845, 98.103, 98.879, 98.879, 98.966, 98.966, 98.966,
       99.310, 99.310] + [99.397] * 16 + [99.655] * 16
n = [10 * (k + 1) for k in range(len(cov))]

plt.rcParams.update({'font.size': 10})
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 3.2))
ax.axhline(100 * 1156 / 1160, color='#666666', linestyle='--', linewidth=1)
ax.text(495, 98.8, 'all faults that Fault can detect, 99.66 %', color='#444444',
        ha='right', va='top')
ax.step(n, cov, where='post', color='#08306b', linewidth=2)
ax.plot(n, cov, 'o', color='#08306b', markersize=3)
ax.set_xlim(0, 500)
ax.set_ylim(80, 100.5)
ax.set_xlabel('random test vectors')
ax.set_ylabel('fault coverage (%)')
ax.grid(color='#e5e5e5', linewidth=0.8)
ax.spines[['top', 'right']].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
